title: Grade 4 Science — Thu, Jun 12
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 4 of 5: Minerals, water, and balanced diet
subject: science

questions.question: Minerals are nutrients needed by the body in:
options: No amount — they are not needed
questions.explanation: Minerals like calcium, iron, and iodine are needed in small amounts, but their absence causes deficiency diseases.

questions.question: Which mineral makes our bones and teeth strong?
questions.explanation: Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth. Milk, curd, cheese, and green vegetables are good calcium sources.

questions.question: Iron is needed in the body to:
options: Make haemoglobin in blood which carries oxygen
questions.explanation: Iron is a component of haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen from lungs to all body cells.

questions.question: Iodine is needed for the proper working of the:
questions.explanation: Iodine is used by the thyroid gland to produce hormones that control growth and metabolism.

questions.question: Water makes up about ____ of our body weight.
questions.explanation: About 60–70% of the human body is water. It is in blood, cells, and all body fluids.

questions.question: Which of these is a function of water in the body?
options: Dissolving and transporting nutrients in blood
questions.explanation: Water dissolves nutrients and carries them in the blood to all cells. It also removes waste through urine and sweat.

questions.question: A balanced diet contains:
options: All five nutrients in right amounts along with water and fibre
questions.explanation: A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and fibre in right proportions.

questions.question: The food pyramid or food plate helps us understand:
options: How much of each food group we should eat daily
questions.explanation: The food pyramid/plate shows recommended portions of different food groups for a balanced daily diet.

questions.question: Sodium (salt) in the body is needed to:
options: Regulate body fluids and nerve signals
questions.explanation: Sodium regulates fluid balance, helps nerves and muscles function, and maintains blood pressure.

questions.question: Drinking at least how many glasses of water per day is recommended?
questions.explanation: Health experts recommend about 8 glasses (approximately 2 litres) of water per day for an average person.

questions.question: Phosphorus is a mineral that works with calcium to build:
questions.explanation: Phosphorus, along with calcium, forms the hard mineral structure of bones and teeth.

questions.question: Which of these provides multiple nutrients: protein, calcium, fat, and vitamins A and B?
questions.explanation: Milk is a near-complete food — it provides protein, calcium, fats, and vitamins A and B12, especially for growing children.

questions.question: Junk food like chips and cola lack:
questions.explanation: Junk foods are 'empty calories' — they have carbohydrates and fat but lack essential vitamins, minerals, protein, and fibre.

questions.question: What happens if we do not drink enough water?
options: We get dehydrated — feeling thirsty, dizzy, and tired
questions.explanation: Dehydration occurs when the body loses more water than it takes in. Symptoms include thirst, headache, dizziness, and fatigue.

questions.question: A meal of dal, rice, sabzi, curd, and salad is considered balanced because:
options: It has only one food group
It contains protein (dal), carbs (rice), vitamins (sabzi/salad), and calcium (curd)
questions.explanation: A typical Indian thali with dal+rice+vegetables+curd covers proteins, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and calcium.
